## Mechanism: why directional traversal destroys gold@4

Measured directly from `tuning/query_reformulation_v2_raw/arm_{D,E}_per_question.jsonl`
(recomputable with the snippet in "Reproducing" below):

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| arm D vs E, rank-0 (anchor) frame identical | 2676/2685 = 0.9966 |
| mean overlap between top-4(D) and top-4(E) | 1.30 of 4 |
| median top-4 timestamp spread, arm A | 11.51 s |
| median top-4 timestamp spread, arm D | 12.11 s |
| median top-4 timestamp spread, arm E | **0.67 s** |
| arm E questions where traversal changed the frame count | 2588/2685 |
| gold@4 on those questions, D -> E | 0.5363 -> 0.3369 |

`traverse_directional` (iris/temporal_traversal.py:176) does not *add* context
around the retrieved set -- it **replaces** the ranked set. It rebuilds the
candidate pool from `index.frames` inside the time window and re-sorts it by
`_direction_score` (recency / scene continuity / position prior / action score /
codec confidence / target similarity), a score with no semantic-retrieval term
except the optional target-similarity blend. The anchor is pinned to rank 0
(`1e6` sentinel), so anchor@1 is preserved almost exactly (0.3028 in both D and
E), but the original semantic ranks 1-3 are evicted and replaced by the anchor's
temporal neighbours.

The result is that the top-4 collapses from a diverse ~12 s spread to a ~0.67 s
huddle around one frame. Because gold@4 rewards *any* of four frames landing
inside a gold span, four near-simultaneous frames behave like a single sample.
That is the whole -19.7 pp effect, and it is a design consequence, not noise --
the same collapse hits the legacy symmetric expansion (arm C, -13.3 pp).

This also explains the duration-bucket pattern: arm E's damage is worst on short
gold spans (`<2s`: 0.3417 -> 0.1619) and mildest on long ones (`>=10s`: 0.7604 ->
0.5717), exactly as a loss-of-coverage effect should behave.

## Parser diagnostics -- interpretation

The pre-registered hypothesis was "if the fallback path dominates val_tune, V2 is
mostly inert". The measured picture is more specific than that:

- `relation_source` is **never** `lexical` and never `fallback`: every val_tune
  question carries a NExT-QA type code, so the type code decides the relation
  100% of the time. The `relation` histogram is exactly the type histogram
  (CAUSE=1172=CW, MANNER=392=CH, AFTER=704=TN, DURING=380=TC, BEFORE=37=TP).
  The temporal-vocabulary work in section 6 contributes **nothing** to relation
  selection on this split; 344 questions (12.8%) are logged `conflict`, where
  lexical cues disagreed with the type code and were overridden.
- Clause extraction, which is what actually shapes the *prompts*, fails outright
  on 644/2685 (24.0%) with `no_clause_pattern_matched`, concentrated in CW
  (324/1172 = 27.6%) and TC (183/380 = 48.2%).
- 1272/2685 (47.4%) of questions yield only ONE embedding text, i.e. no
  anchor/target decomposition happened at all.
- `occurrence_selector` fires on 12/2685 (0.45%) -- effectively dead code on this
  split. `position_prior` fires on 440/2685 (16.4%).

So V2's retrieval-side behaviour on val_tune is: a type-code lookup (which needs
none of the parser), plus a prompt rewrite that is a no-op or near-no-op for
roughly half the split. Arm D (structured_v2, no traversal) landing at +0.0045
gold@4 with a CI spanning zero is exactly what that predicts.

## Acceptance bar

| criterion | result | met? |
|---|---|---|
| real gain in gold-frame@4 | D +0.0045 (CI [-0.0134,+0.0220]); E -0.1974 (CI [-0.2164,-0.1788]) | **NO** |
| real gain in mIoP | every arm <= A; E -0.0113, D -0.0038, none significant positive | **NO** |
| no material mIoU regression | A 0.1609 -> D 0.1604 (ok), E 0.1527 (-0.0081) | partial |
| no gain attributable to degenerate spans | 0 zero-width and 0 invalid spans in all 5 arms; mean span width flat (4.29 -> 4.25 s) | n/a (no gain to attribute) |
| gains not confined to one question type | no gains anywhere; E regresses on all five types | **NO** |
| structured p95 latency <= ~1.5x baseline | A 4.66 ms -> E 4.98 ms = 1.07x | **YES** |
| <= 1 PPR call per query | D/E exactly 1.000 (max 1); legacy B/C 3.93 (max 5) | **YES** |

Two of seven met. The two that pass are the engineering-efficiency claims, and
they hold cleanly: structured_v2 is ~3.6x cheaper per query than legacy
(4.07 ms vs 14.73 ms median) at 1 PPR call instead of 3.93, and the <=3
embedding budget is respected (mean 1.54, max 3, 0 over budget). The embedding
cache hit rate is low (9.55%) because val_tune questions are near-unique; the
cache is sized for repeated production queries, not a single-pass sweep.

**Verdict: the ablation does not support V2. The implementation is NOT ready for
a val_confirm run.**

## Reproducing

Every number above recomputes from the committed per-question JSONL:

```
python scripts/query_reformulation_v2_ablation.py --arms A,B,C,D,E
```

Raw artifacts: `tuning/query_reformulation_v2_raw/arm_{A,B,C,D,E}_per_question.jsonl`
(2685 rows each), `tuning/query_reformulation_v2_ablation.csv` (arm x scope x
metric), `tuning/query_reformulation_v2_parser_diagnostics.json`,
`tuning/query_reformulation_v2_parser_audit.csv` (100 questions, 20 per type).
